```{r}
#| label: corpus-dataset-jsonld
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# schema.org/Dataset markup describing the IRW corpus as a whole.
# ben-domingue/irw#1706, minimal pilot -- see that issue's 2026-09-03 comments.
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS: the IRW has no presence in Google Dataset Search, which
# indexes pages carrying schema.org/Dataset JSON-LD. Nothing on this site carried
# any. This is the smallest thing that tests whether the IRW can be indexed at
# all: one block, no new URLs, no per-table pages. To undo it, delete the
# {{< include >}} line in data.qmd -- nothing else references it.
#
# IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT A CATALOG. Strictly the IRW is a DataCatalog of many
# Datasets, but Dataset Search indexes Dataset and ignores DataCatalog, so the
# corpus is described as one Dataset that names the catalog it belongs to. The
# per-table pages proposed in #1706 use the same shape, so the two agree if
# those ever ship.
#
# NO DATE IS COMPUTED HERE. datePublished comes from the version manifest, never
# from Sys.Date(): a date that moves on every render is not a fact about the data.

local({
  # Loaded here rather than relying on another include: this block sits near the
  # top of data.qmd, before _load-data.qmd has run.
  suppressMessages({ library(redivis); library(jsonlite) })
  if (!nzchar(Sys.getenv("REDIVIS_API_TOKEN"))) return(invisible(NULL))

  info <- tryCatch({
    # The manifest is authoritative for the corpus version (ARCHITECTURE.md rule 1);
    # this reads it rather than restating anything from it.
    con <- url(paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ben-domingue/irw/main/",
                      "metadata/version_manifest.tsv"))
    on.exit(try(close(con), silent = TRUE), add = TRUE)
    m <- utils::read.delim(con, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, colClasses = "character")
    m$irw_version <- as.integer(m$irw_version)
    v <- max(m$irw_version)
    # numRows off the table's properties: a metadata read, not an export, so it
    # costs nothing against the Redivis export quota.
    #
    # This is the DOCUMENTED corpus -- nrow(metadata), the same denominator
    # 11_status.R uses for n_tables. It trails the live table count by up to a
    # week by construction, because metadata.csv only moves when the weekly
    # pipeline runs (4,134 documented against 4,221 live on 2026-09-03; see the
    # 2026-09-03 block on ben-domingue/irw#1702). Describing the documented
    # corpus is the honest choice: those are the tables the metadata can
    # actually describe.
    n <- redivis$user("datapages")$dataset("irw_meta:bdxt")$
           table("metadata:h5gs")$get()$properties$numRows
    list(version = v,
         released = substr(m$irw_released_at[m$irw_version == v][1], 1, 10),
         n_tables = as.integer(n))
  }, error = function(e) NULL)

  if (is.null(info)) return(invisible(NULL))

  site <- "https://itemresponsewarehouse.org"
  d <- list(
    "@context"      = "https://schema.org/",
    "@type"         = "Dataset",
    name            = "Item Response Warehouse",
    alternateName   = "IRW",
    description     = paste0(
      "The Item Response Warehouse (IRW) is a harmonised collection of ",
      format(info$n_tables, big.mark = ","), " item response datasets, ",
      "reformatted to a single standard so that item-level response data from ",
      "education, psychology and health research can be analysed together. ",
      "Every table gives one row per person-item response, with consistent ",
      "identifier, item and response columns, plus covariates where available. ",
      "The corpus supports psychometric and item response theory research, ",
      "measurement invariance work, and methodological studies that need many ",
      "datasets rather than one. Access is free, via a browser, an R package ",
      "or a Python package. This description is of IRW v", info$version, "."),
    url             = paste0(site, "/data.html"),
    identifier      = paste0(site, "/data.html"),
    version         = paste0("IRW v", info$version),
    datePublished   = info$released,
    isAccessibleForFree = TRUE,
    license         = paste0(
      "Licences are recorded per table and vary by source; see each table's ",
      "record in the IRW metadata."),
    citation        = paste0(
      "Domingue, B. W., et al. (2025). An introduction to the Item Response ",
      "Warehouse (IRW): A resource for enhancing data usage in psychometrics. ",
      "Behavior Research Methods. https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-025-02796-y"),
    keywords        = c("item response theory", "psychometrics",
                        "educational measurement", "item response data",
                        "test data", "survey data", "measurement",
                        "assessment", "latent variable models"),
    creator         = list("@type" = "Organization",
                           name = "Item Response Warehouse", url = site),
    publisher       = list("@type" = "Organization",
                           name = "Redivis", url = "https://redivis.com"),
    includedInDataCatalog = list("@type" = "DataCatalog",
                                 name = "Item Response Warehouse", url = site),
    distribution    = list(list(
      "@type" = "DataDownload",
      name = "IRW datasets on Redivis",
      encodingFormat = "text/csv",
      contentUrl = "https://redivis.com/datasets/as2e-cv7jb41fd/tables"))
  )

  cat("<script type=\"application/ld+json\">\n",
      jsonlite::toJSON(d, auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE), "\n</script>\n",
      sep = "")
})
```
